entries.title: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure and charters out tankers into October, sources say
entries.claimSummary: QatarEnergy extended force majeure for LNG supplies to several Asian buyers into mid-September.
extractedFacts: Force-majeure notices due to expire in August and early September were extended until mid-September.
Affected buyers include customers in South Korea, India and Bangladesh.
QatarEnergy continued leasing some LNG tankers through mid-October.
At least nine QELM/QET-controlled LNG carriers were sub-chartered to named third parties.
entries.carryReason: Reviewed Sep 11; the Reuters July 23 notice remains a valid historical disclosure, but no newer source-approved replacement is available in this evidence record. Keep the later extension as carried manual context.

entries.title: QatarEnergy seeks US LNG deals through to 2031, sources say
entries.claimSummary: Reuters reported that QatarEnergy is seeking replacement US LNG through 2031 after Iranian strikes damaged Ras Laffan capacity, while force-majeure notices have been renewed through November.
extractedFacts: Two of Ras Laffan's 14 LNG trains and the gas-to-liquids facility were damaged, with 12.8 million tonnes per annum sidelined for an estimated three to five years.
QatarEnergy's force-majeure notices were renewed monthly, most recently through November, with further extensions possible.
QatarEnergy Trading was seeking 2-3 million tonnes per annum of US LNG through 2031 to replace damaged capacity.
entries.carryReason: Reviewed Sep 18; this manual-reviewed Reuters event remains the latest approved QatarEnergy force-majeure and replacement-supply update because no automated QatarEnergy endpoint is approved; no newer replacement was found in today's review.

entries.title: Strait of Hormuz Crossings Rise 8% Week-on-Week, But Dark AIS Activity Remains Elevated
entries.claimSummary: Kpler vessel-type data reported via Foreign Policy Journal shows 3 LNG tanker transits among 106 total Hormuz crossings during Jul 27-Aug 2, the first LNG-specific movement since the carried July 18 zero-transit observation.
extractedFacts: The week of Jul 27-Aug 2 recorded 106 total crossings by 96 distinct vessels, up 8% from 98 crossings the prior week.
Vessel-type breakdown of the 106 crossings included 3 LNG tankers, 40 liquid tankers, 24 bulk carriers, and smaller counts of other vessel types.
Dark AIS activity (undetermined routes) covered 41% of crossings, down from 49% the prior week.
entries.carryReason: Reviewed Sep 20; no newer source-verified weekly Kpler LNG-transit breakdown is approved, so retain the Aug 3 count of 3 LNG transits for the week of Jul 27-Aug 2.

entries.title: US, Iran engaged in tanker war: Where is the months-long conflict headed?
entries.claimSummary: Al Jazeera reported the US and Iran fought a direct tanker war Sep 5-6: CENTCOM struck three Iranian oil tankers while Iran fired missiles at a US carrier and destroyer and hit three tankers plus three US-linked vessels.
extractedFacts: CENTCOM struck three Iranian oil tankers near Kharg Island, near Jask, and an unladen vessel in the Gulf of Oman after crew evacuation, with no US personnel injured.
Iran launched ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and destroyer, both of which evaded the missiles.
Iran targeted three oil tankers in the Strait and three US-linked vessels elsewhere, and separately claimed to have struck an unmanned US vessel.
CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper warned of an even higher economic cost for further attacks, while Iran's IRGC warned vessels not to transit unauthorised waterways.
entries.carryReason: Reviewed Sep 20; Al Jazeera's Sep 6 report remains the latest approved direct security evidence of the tanker war. The National's Sep 14 report confirms talks were shelved and no newer source confirms a signed commercial reopening or verified Hormuz route clearance.

entries.title: Saudi offers more crude via Oman loading after pipeline attacks, sources say
entries.claimSummary: Reuters reported Sep 16 that Saudi Aramco is offering more crude via ship-to-ship transfer off Oman's Sohar port after drone attacks damaged the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea, doubling loadings at Ras Tanura and Juaymah.
extractedFacts: Saudi Aramco offered its Arab Light, Arab Medium and Arab Heavy grades to Asian term buyers for loading off Sohar, outside the Strait of Hormuz.
A satellite image dated Sep 13 showed damage at the Saudi East-West pipeline from a strike that hit it on September 11, 2026.
Saudi Arabia doubled daily crude loadings at Ras Tanura and Juaymah terminals to about two VLCCs (4 million barrels) over the past week, per Energy Aspects satellite tracking.
Kpler shiptracking showed four VLCCs (8 million barrels combined) loading at Ras Tanura on Wednesday, Sep 16.

Saudi Arabia shut the East-West pipeline on Friday, Sep 11 after drone-attack damage, and informed European customers some September-loading cargoes would be cancelled while Yanbu loadings were suspended.

entries.title: US-Iran conflict helps drive wave of supertanker orders
entries.claimSummary: Reuters reported Sep 17 that Strait of Hormuz tanker crossings remain in single digits (LSEG data) as shipowners order a record wave of VLCCs to serve longer Atlantic-to-Asia routes.
extractedFacts: Shipowners ordered 217 Very Large Crude Carriers in 2026 so far, versus 93 in all of 2025, a buying spree worth over $20 billion, per Signal Group data.
Allied Shipbroking recorded 164 VLCC orders in 2026, up from 83 in 2025.

An LSEG chart of Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic (vessels above 10,000 deadweight tonnes) showed crossings remaining in single digits, with the article headline noting crossings remain in single digits.
VLCC spot prices have climbed above $500,000 per day, up from about $132,000 in February before the war, per Allied Shipbroking.
Gulf producers are increasingly shuttling oil out of the Gulf through Hormuz to reload onto larger tankers waiting in the Gulf of Oman, tying up vessels and adding to VLCC demand.
